(right). 3.4 Planned and Recent Building Upgrades Moore Street Seniors, Inc., is pursuing a renovation of the building to update it to be more energy efficient and healthy. As part of this renovation, Moore Street Seniors, Inc., has already: • Started to convert lighting to efficient LED lamps. Hallway and common areas have been converted. • Replaced the fuel oil boiler with a Burnham natural gas boiler, model # V904A, additionally with a Power Flame Burner, model # C1-GO-10, with conversion completed and the new heating system commissioned in October 2023 (see Figure 4). • Obtained State of Alaska funding for the replacement of all the windows in the building. This is expected to reduce air leakage in the building and save energy, with a timeline to complete the window replacements by the end of 2027. Moore Street Seniors, Inc. requested the funding due to residents’ complaints about drafts through the windows, and windows icing over in the cold winter months. 5 This report is available at no cost from the National Laboratory of the Rockies (NLR) at www.nlr.gov/publications. 3.5 Building Baseline – ENERGY STAR Portfolio Manager NLR staff created an ENERGY STAR Portfolio Manager (ESPM) profile for Moore Street Senior Apartments. ESPM is a free software program created and maintained by the United States Environmental Protection Agency. It allows building owners and others to track building metrics and energy use for properties, and it also calculates several different metrics that building owners can use to benchmark their property and then see improvements as retrofits are completed. Shown in Table 2 is the energy performance profile created in ESPM. To establish a baseline year, ESPM utilizes the first complete year of energy bills entered into the software, in this case starting in 2023. Similarly, the energy current year is based on the most recent full year of energy bills entered, for the calendar year of 2024. This profile includes Moore Street Seniors, Inc.’s electricity, natural gas, and fuel oil consumption (before the natural gas conversion). The metrics reported are defined as follows2: Site Energy Use Intensity (EUI) is the measure of how much energy a building uses in kilo British thermal units per square foot of space over a year (kBtu/ft2/yr. It is calculated using the energy consumed by the building on-site (electricity, natural gas, fuel oil) and does not include the energy associated with the generation of the energy at the source.
